correctness.rationale: The proof reconstructs the two quadratic-regularized model minima with the factors 1/(2 alpha) and g/(2 sqrt(F)) unchanged. The exact radial prox minimum is on [0,r], and the NGN envelope is F/(1+alpha g^2/(2F)). In the convex-square-root branch the proof separates positive and negative affine tangents at t0=r-2F/g and lower-bounds every exact prox candidate by the NGN minimum. In the concave branch the squared tangent majorizes the loss on [0,r]; if the NGN minimizer exits through t<0, an explicit inequality shows the exact-proximal center candidate still has smaller envelope. p-power strictness follows from strict tangent inequalities; the small- and large-alpha limits are derived from the exact prox scalar equation, including the nonsmooth p=1 case. The packaged verify.py returned VERIFY_OK 702 cases; tests were not used as an infinite proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: A general lower-surrogate theorem does not directly cover this claim: when the square root is convex the affine tangent becomes negative near the center, so its square is not everywhere a lower surrogate; when it is concave the unrestricted NGN minimizer can pass the center. These two obstructions are treated by new explicit case arguments. General convergence rates for either method alone do not imply ordering of their one-step index minima.

originality.rationale: The 2026 source introduces the NGN and SPP stability indices and compares them separately with SGD, while its Appendix A.3 computes equality only for isotropic quadratics. The current theorem provides a new all-stepsize inter-method sign criterion from square-root radial curvature, including both strict reversal regimes, the center-crossing proof, and explicit signed asymptotic laws for power losses. Orvieto-Xiao 2024 derives NGN itself but does not make this NGN-versus-exact-proximal-index comparison. The available 2025 momentum paper is about a different algorithm. Not a claim of exhaustive uniqueness: unindexed equivalent general-surrogate literature is a residual risk.

value.rationale: The 2026 stability-index framework evaluates NGN and SPP separately relative to SGD; a cross-method ranking is not universal. The radial shape theorem identifies a natural, verifiable geometric criterion yielding a global-in-step-parameter ranking, explicitly handles model-root and minimizer crossing (where naive Jensen or surrogate logic fails), and locates the exact reversal at the quadratic homogeneity p=2. Two signed asymptotic coefficients quantify the discrepancy and supply robust benchmark regimes for analyzing models. The result is structural rather than a cosmetic reparameterization, and no broader algorithmic claim is asserted.
